extracted.intended_audience: patent proprietors, patent applicants and registered patent agents (users of the Singapore patent register/IPOS)
extracted.subtask_description: Official procedural guidance for post‑grant patent actions in Singapore: rules and criteria for renewal payments and reminders, lapse and expiry handling, patent term extension (including unreasonable delay and pharmaceutical curtailment), post‑grant amendment procedures (including assessment criteria and opposition), and restoration of lapsed patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal when patent not due or already renewed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent is not due for renewal or has already been renewed, the Formalities officer will refuse the renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon refusal a refund request will be initiated; applicant may reply via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal when patent has lapsed (renewal non-payment) and restoration invite
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent has lapsed due to non‑payment of renewal fees, the Formalities officer will refuse the renewal application and invite the applicant to request restoration by filing Patents Form 19 together with a Statutory Declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon refusal a refund request will be initiated; see Chapter 9.4 for restoration information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal for insufficient payment due to miscalculation
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is insufficient payment due to miscalculation of the renewal fees payable, the Formalities officer will refuse the application and invite the applicant to put in a new request with the correct fees as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon refusal a refund job will be initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated renewal notifications are advisory only
rubrics_metrics.description: The system will automatically issue a notification to the renewal agent on record or the last person who renewed the patent to inform that the window for renewal is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional service to assist proprietors in case of breakdown of their own tracking systems; the absence of this letter is not a valid reason for missing renewal and does not entitle payment after the prescribed period without additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overdue renewal second reminder and status update
rubrics_metrics.description: If the renewal payment is overdue, the system will automatically issue a second notification to the renewal agent or last renewer informing that the payment is overdue and the consequences of non‑payment; the person will be invited to renew with late fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the same time, the patent status will be updated to 'Lapsed (late renewal possible)'. If the second reminder was not issued within 1 month from the due date, the Registry will extend the timeline to allow payment of the renewal fees within 2 months with no additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent status change to 'Lapsed (restoration possible)' at 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The system will update the status of the patent to 'Lapsed (restoration possible)' at the end of 6 months following the renewal date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entry will be made in the register and Patents Journal and a notification sent to proprietor or authorized agent inviting restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent status change to 'Lapsed' at 18 months if not restored
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of 18 months from the renewal due date (for renewals due on or after 14 Feb 2014), if the patent has not been restored and no restoration request is pending, the patent status will be updated to 'Lapsed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter 9.4 for restoration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and expiry of patent (20 years and possible extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent is 20 years from the date of filing; a patent may expire at the end of that term unless a patent term extension is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a term extension is approved the patent expires at the end of the extended term. The system will update status to 'Expired' once term is up, enter an entry in the register and publish in the Patents Journal. Expiry is effective as of the original expiry date even if entered later; expiry will not be entered while restoration, term extension or surrender requests are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to apply for patent term extension (post‑2004 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents granted for applications with a date of filing on or after 1 Jul 2004, the proprietor may apply to extend the term of a patent beyond 20 years by filing Patents Form 54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds and timelines for extension are set out in rules and Section 36A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for patent term extension — Registrar delay
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension may be granted where there was an unreasonable delay by the Registrar in granting the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definition of 'unreasonable delay' and calculation of extension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for extension — corresponding/patent office extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension may be granted where the patent was granted on the basis of prescribed documents relating to a corresponding application or related national phase application and there was an unreasonable delay in the issue of the corresponding patent and that other patent office has extended the corresponding patent's term on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the existence of delay and corresponding office's extension are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for extension — pharmaceutical curtailment
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension may be granted where the patent subject includes a substance that is an active ingredient of a pharmaceutical product and there was unreasonable curtailment of the opportunity to exploit the patent caused by the process of obtaining marketing approval for the first pharmaceutical product using that substance, provided the term has not previously been extended for this ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional documentary proof and limits on prior extensions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines to apply for extension (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: For unreasonable Registrar delay or corresponding patent delay/extension, the applicant may apply within 6 months from the date of grant of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate timelines for pharmaceutical‑approval ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines to apply for extension (pharmaceutical ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pharmaceutical curtailment, the applicant may apply within 6 months from the date of grant or the date marketing approval was obtained, whichever is later; not later than 6 months before the end of the 20‑year term; and while the patent is still in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three timing conditions must be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'unreasonable delay by the Registrar'
rubrics_metrics.description: A delay by the Registrar is not 'unreasonable' unless: (a) the interval between filing date and issue of Certificate of Grant, excluding any period attributable to an act or omission of the applicant, exceeds 4 years; or (b) the interval between filing a Request for Search and Examination (Form 11) or Request for Examination (Form 12) and issue of Certificate of Grant, excluding applicant‑attributable periods, exceeds 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both A and B conditions are separately described; applicant‑attributable periods are excluded from calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant‑attributable periods (what counts as applicant delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period 'attributable to an act or omission of the applicant' includes numerous specific delays (without prejudice to generality), such as: the time to pay filing fees, time to make required observations, time to file earlier‑application documents, time to file claims, time to respond to formal requirements or invitations to amend, time to request and pay for search/examination/reports, time to respond to written opinions, time to apply for reviews, time to satisfy grant fee conditions, time to enter national phase, time to rectify failures to comply, and any extensions granted on applicant request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A long detailed list (items a through u) enumerates typical applicant delays used to exclude from Registrar delay calculations; includes periods for prosecution actions, responses, and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curtailment test for pharmaceutical subject
rubrics_metrics.description: A curtailment of opportunity to exploit a patent (subject includes active ingredient of pharmaceutical) caused by obtaining marketing approval shall not be treated as unreasonable unless: (a) marketing approval was obtained after the date of issue of the Certificate of Grant; and (b) the interval between application for marketing approval and obtaining approval, excluding periods attributable to applicant for marketing approval, exceeds 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test focuses on the marketing‑approval timeline and excludes applicant‑caused delays in the marketing‑approval process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary certificate for marketing approval dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should submit to the Registrar a certificate from the relevant authority stating the date the application for marketing approval was filed, the date marketing approval was obtained, and for each period attributable to an act or omission of the applicant for marketing approval the dates on which such periods started and ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certificate supports pharmaceutical‑ground extension claims (Rule 51A(9)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant‑attributable periods for marketing approval
rubrics_metrics.description: For marketing approval, periods attributable to an act or omission of the applicant for marketing approval include the time to correct deficiencies, time to respond to requests for clarification/information, and any extensions granted by the relevant authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These periods are excluded when assessing the >2 year marketing approval interval (Rule 51A(11)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of extension period for Registrar unreasonable delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the unreasonable delay is the interval exceeding the thresholds, the period of extension equals the period by which the relevant interval exceeds the threshold (e.g., interval exceeds 4 years → extension = excess over 4 years; interval exceeds 2 years for requests → extension = excess over 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A table in the rules sets the mapping between period of unreasonable delay and period of extension; if both A and B apply the relevant calculations are combined as described in the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of extension period for curtailment (pharmaceutical)
rubrics_metrics.description: For unreasonable curtailment, the period of extension is the shortest of: i) the interval between issue of Certificate of Grant and the date marketing approval was obtained; ii) the period by which the interval between application and obtaining marketing approval (excluding applicant attributable periods) exceeds 2 years; or iii) a period of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This caps and limits extension periods for pharmaceutical curtailment claims (Rule 51A(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer initial checks for extension application
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an extension request the Formalities officer will review: fee paid; date of filing is on or after 1 Jul 2004; patent is still in force; names of patentees on form correspond with records; representation details/address for service correspond (else file CM1/CM2); form filed within required timelines; documentary evidence and/or certificate submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, applicant invited to clarify or rectify within 2 months; corrections via Form CM4 or representation updates via CM1/CM2; reply via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal where extension requirements not met
rubrics_metrics.description: If the objections to an extension application cannot be overcome or there is no response within the time period, the Formalities officer will refuse the application and notify the proprietor; refusal will be entered as an event in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up includes reminders; see correction routes (CM4, CM1/CM2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and certificate of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application satisfies all requirements, the Formalities officer will approve the extension request and send the 'Certificate of Extension of Patent Term' to the proprietor; the approval will be entered as an event on the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate is the formal outcome and will affect expiry handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted post‑grant amendments constraint (no added matter/no scope extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may make voluntary amendments to the specification after grant provided that the amendment does not disclose any additional matter or extend the scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments allow refinement to overcome newly discovered prior art and are deemed always to have had effect from grant of the patent (Section 38, Rule 52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedure for amendment after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: To amend the specification after grant the proprietor may file Patents Form 17 together with supporting documents setting out reasons for amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 1 Apr 2017 both marked‑up amendments and clean copies of amended sheets are required; from 1 Dec 2019, if claims amended, a marked‑up and clean copy of the full set of claims must be submitted; amendments should be based on latest specification on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting evidence and reasons for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient evidence setting out fully the reasons for amendments, circumstances leading to amendments and any supporting evidence should be submitted; if there is undue delay, the proprietor will be requested to submit reasons for the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay may affect acceptability and may trigger requests for explanatory material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criteria for post‑grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑grant amendments will be assessed on whether relevant matters are sufficiently disclosed; whether there was any unreasonable delay in seeking amendments; and whether the patentee has gained an unfair advantage by delaying amendments known to be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria align with UK guidelines and Singapore High Court decisions cited (e.g., Ship’s Equipment Centre Bremen GmbH v Fuji Trading; Warner‑Lambert v Novartis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checks for amendment application
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt the Formalities officer will review: fee paid; patent is granted (else use Form 13); patent is in force (if lapsed, options include renew with late fees or request restoration if within allowable time); representation details/address for service correspond with record (else file CM1/CM2); no pending proceedings before Court or Registrar affecting validity; reason for amendments submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, invite clarification within 2 months; corrections via CM4, CM1/CM2; reply via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to Patent Examiner and timelines for responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If all requirements are met, the Formalities officer forwards the request to the Patent Examiner for review and notifies the proprietor. If the Examiner requires additional supporting documents or clarification, the Formalities officer will send the Examiner’s comments to the proprietor and invite clarification within 2 months; if no response the request will be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Examiner objects, a Notification of Intention to Refuse is issued; applicant may request to be heard by filing Form HC4 within 1 month from that notification; for partial objections the applicant may be asked to submit a revised amendment limited to allowable parts within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting leave to amend and publication for opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Patent Examiner is satisfied that the amendments can be allowed, the Formalities officer will grant leave to amend the specification; the amended specification will be published in the Patents Journal for opposition and the application for amendment will be entered as an event in the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers opposition timelines and public availability of the amended specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure against amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may oppose the application to amend the specification by filing a notice of opposition via Patents Form 58 within 2 months from the date of the advertisement, accompanied by a statement setting out the facts relied upon for opposition and the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opposition is filed, IPOS Hearings & Mediation Dept will communicate outcome; a successful opposition leads to refusal and register entry; unsuccessful opposition results in invitation to file the new specification as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing new specification as amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Where invited to file the new specification, the applicant must submit it within 2 months from the Notification to file New Specification as Amended; the new specification must incorporate the approved amendments and no new amendments or corrections may be introduced except formalities (e.g., page numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new specification is not in order, the Formalities officer will invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months; corrections via Form CM4; representation updates via CM1/CM2; clarifications via eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal or approval outcome for amendment application
rubrics_metrics.description: If objections cannot be overcome or there is no response, the application to amend will be refused and the refusal will be entered as an event in the register. When all requirements are met and objections overcome, the Formalities officer will approve the request, update the approval as an event, and make the new specification available on public search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and public search reflect final outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration eligibility — overall principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent ceases to have effect at the end of the prescribed period for payment of renewal fee if not paid; the patent status is updated to 'Lapsed (Restoration possible)' once the due date to pay renewal fees with late payment fees has expired (i.e., within 6 months after the renewal due date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is possible within the allowed period subject to demonstrating lapse was unintentional; third parties' rights are protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration window (18 months) and unintentionality test
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to restore the patent within 18 months (for patents lapsed on or after 14 Feb 2014) if the proprietor can demonstrate that the lapse of the patent was unintentional. The unintentional test applies to the proprietor or any person entitled to the patent at the time when renewal fees were payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties' accrued rights are protected; reference to required Statutory Declaration sample in Appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and evidential requirement for restoration (Form 19 + Statutory Declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may request restoration by filing Patents Form 19 together with a Statutory Declaration (or affidavit). For patents lapsed on/after 14 Feb 2014, restoration is allowable if the Registrar is satisfied the failure to pay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sample Statutory Declaration is provided in the Appendix; the Formalities officer will review the declaration's content against the unintentionality test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checks for restoration application
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt the Formalities officer will review: fee paid; patent has lapsed; form filed within 18 months after renewal due date; Statutory Declaration/affidavit submitted within 14 days from receipt of Patents Form 19; applicant for restoration is proprietor or person entitled to the patent at time renewal was payable; and review the Statutory Declaration to determine whether the lapse was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not met, officer will invite clarification/rectification within 2 months and may request a supplementary statutory declaration if reasons are unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and communication routes for restoration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: To rectify errors applicants may file Form CM4 indicating relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91); to update representation/address for service file Form CM1 or CM2; to submit clarification letters, supplementary Statutory Declarations and evidence reply via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines for responses are strict; reminders will be issued where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal when restoration requirements not met or period elapsed
rubrics_metrics.description: If formal objections cannot be overcome or there is no response within the time period, the Formalities officer will refuse the restoration request. If the period for restoration has passed, the status of the patent will be updated to 'Lapsed'. If restoration is still possible, status remains 'Lapsed (restoration possible)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal is entered in register; keep track of restoration windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement, advertisement and status update for restoration applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If all formal requirements are met the Formalities officer will acknowledge and advertise the restoration application; the advertisement will be entered as an event in the register and published in the next Patents Journal, and the patent status updated to 'Lapsed (restoration pending)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advertisement constitutes the notice required by Section 39(4) and concludes the period where a person who began in good faith acts that would otherwise infringe may continue to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment requirement upon provisional satisfaction for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Formalities officer is satisfied that the restoration application can be allowed, the proprietor will be notified to pay the additional fee for restoration and all unpaid renewal fees within 2 months from date of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment within that time is required for restoration to be completed.
